title: Monitor file, v0
description: One file of InOrbit monitors in a project's .inorbit/monitors/ folder (RFC 0008), read as JSON. It is the InOrbit agent's checks.toml format (core RFC 0040.1 and 0040.2; dataplane crates/iohr-agent/src/checks_file.rs): [[check]] entries the agent runs and expects to pass, and [[refuse]] entries it expects to be refused. This schema holds the shapes and bounds; the rules it cannot say (which keys go with which surface, every between 60s and 24h, URLs, names unique across files) are checked by iohr monitors check. A cli check (target = { cli = "app" }) runs the project's own built binary with argv, never a shell, in a throwaway folder that is removed after the run; the InOrbit agent has no cli surface yet, so iohr monitors export and install leave cli checks out (RFC 0008).

refuse.description: A monitor that should be refused: by the agent's policy, by the platform, or by the service with the answer in expect.

name.description: Unique across every [[check]] and [[refuse]] the agent reads.

surface.description: How it is checked. Left out, a URL is http, host:port is tcp and { cli = ... } is cli. sse, ws, mqtt, mcp, graphql and grpc must be named in the policy's [work] surfaces. ws speaks InOrbit's /v1/ws frames only.

fail_after.description: Failed runs in a row before it is down. 2 for a check, 1 for a refuse, when left out.

auth.description: A reference to the secret, never the secret.

enabled.description: iohr monitors only: false means off by default, for a check only some setups run (such as a second instance of the service). iohr monitors enable turns it on on one machine; export and install leave the entry out, since the agent refuses the key (ADR 0009).

method.description: http (GET when left out), ws and grpc (needed there).

body.description: http: the request body, at most 8 KiB as JSON.

headers.description: http: request headers; only accept and content-type.

events.description: sse: data events to wait for; 1 when left out.

steps.description: cli: steps run in order in one throwaway folder, such as a write verb then a read verb; each has its own argv and expect. The entry's expect then holds only max_ms.

network.description: cli: let the binary reach the network. Left out, every proxy variable points at a closed port.

argv.description: cli: the arguments after the binary, passed as they are, never through a shell. {tmp}, {home} and the copies the runner names (iohr monitors: {board}, {monitors}) are replaced by paths in the throwaway folder.

target.description: A URL (http), host:port (tcp), a bare host (tls, port 443), or a table.

cli.description: The binary, resolved by the runner to the one just built; never a path.

status.description: http, sse, mcp and graphql. Left out, any status under 400 passes.

max_ms.description: The slowest pass; for cli also the deadline, after which the binary is killed (10s when left out).

exit.description: cli: the exit code expected; 0 when left out.

request.description: cli: the JSON Schema the argv must match as a JSON array of strings, after the paths are put in, checked before the binary starts; usually the request part of the verb's schema, schemas/cli/<verb>/v0.json#/$defs/request.

valid_for_days.description: tls and http: days the certificate must still be valid.

headers.description: http: each response header must start with the value given.

shape.description: http, sse and cli (its stdout): the JSON Schema the body must match, read at most 1 MiB, checked in memory and dropped; a failure names only the first mismatch as a location and two types, never a value (core RFC 0040.2, Reading a body). A path such as schemas/api/items/v0.json, or for sse a table of event name to schema path, where an event not named fails. Run by iohr monitors run today; the InOrbit agent does not read bodies yet and refuses this key, so iohr monitors export leaves it out (RFC 0008).

shape_path.description: A schema file under schemas/, or a part of one (#/$defs/<name>).
